sections.h2: Which county holds your Dublin parcel
sections.html:
Dublin sellers can list with an agent, go without one, or take a cash offer, but the first job is the same: find out which county records your parcel. The city spreads across Franklin, Delaware, Union and Madison counties, so deed transfer, valuation and recording follow whichever county holds your deed. Your tax bill or the county auditor's property search will tell you.

Dublin is a Columbus suburb of 49,094 people for July 2025, close to the 49,328 counted in 2020. It covers 24.44 square miles of land. Homes are pricey: the median owner-occupied value is $563,500 and 77.1 percent of the 17,995 households own. Median gross rent is $1,686, and owner costs with a mortgage run $3,055 a month against $1,349 without one. Median household income is $160,296.

sections.h2: Growth and the Bridge Street District
sections.html:
Dublin had 681 residents in 1970 and 3,855 in 1980, then 16,366 in 1990, as Interstate 270 and corporate headquarters arrived. It became a city in August 1987 after passing 5,000 people. The count reached 31,392 in 2000 and 49,328 in 2020, so most houses here are fairly recent construction.

Since 2020 the city has been redeveloping the Bridge Street District, 1,100 acres along the Scioto River with apartments, condominiums, retail and offices, including about 400 apartments and condominiums. Interstate 270 and State Route 161 are the main expressways, and the city is home to company headquarters that draw relocating buyers. If you sell near the district, expect questions about construction and future neighbors.

The Dublin City School District serves the city, and the Hilliard City School District serves a portion of it. Hilliard runs Washington Elementary School inside Dublin's limits. Dublin City has three high schools (Coffman, Scioto and Jerome), five middle schools and fifteen elementary schools.

The attendance boundary for the parcel, not the city name, decides the school. Confirm it before a listing names one.

sections.h2: Permits for work done before a sale
sections.html:
Dublin takes residential permit applications online through its Accela Citizen Access portal and an electronic plan review system. Residential means property with one, two or three family dwelling units. Projects that need permits include:

  • New homes and additions.
  • Interior remodeling, including basement remodels.
  • Decks and porches.
  • Swimming pools and hot tubs.

Fees are paid and the permit issued before work starts, and electrical, HVAC and plumbing contractors must be registered where registration is required. Ohio adds a 1 percent surcharge to residential fees other than plumbing and sewer or water fees. If a past remodel in your house skipped the permit, ask the city's Building Standards office what it takes to close it out before a buyer's inspection.

Dublin enforces zoning, health, parking, nuisance and sign codes. Most violation notices allow ten days to comply, and staff can allow more time in unusual circumstances. Every complaint is investigated first, and nothing follows if no violation turns up. Code Enforcement answers at 614.410.4600.

Zoning and private deed restrictions are separate matters. The city doesn't generally have standing to enforce a deed restriction. In many subdivisions an association does the enforcing, so gather the governing documents and confirm no dues are unpaid before you list. Buyers ask for both.

Renting your house on a short-term basis while it sits on the market is possible only on tight terms and with a city registration. The ordinance passed on October 12, 2020 and applied to operators from November 11, 2020.

Dublin short-term rental rules
RuleRequirement
RegistrationAnnual registration required before listing
Annual fee$225, valid through December 31 of the approval year
Rental limitTwo weeks per calendar year, in up to two increments of seven days
First-offense fine$250 for operating without registering
Primary residence proofTwo of five listed documents, such as a driver's license or utility bill

You also need insurance verification, a notarized affidavit of compliance and a form submitted before each rental period. Post the registration number on any listing.

sections.h2: County deed costs in Delaware County
sections.html:
For the Delaware County part of Dublin, the Recorder charges $39 for the first two pages of a deed, which includes a $5 preservation surcharge, and $8 for each added page. The Auditor's forms page carries the Real Property Conveyance Fee Statement, form DTE 100. Valuation complaints for Delaware County parcels can be filed from January 1, 2027 through March 31, 2027.

Parcels in Franklin or Union County follow those counties' offices. Call the county auditor and recorder for current figures before you budget closing costs.

R.C. 5302.30 requires the owner of a home with one to four units to complete the state disclosure form for the buyer. If the buyer receives it late, after signing a contract, the buyer may cancel in writing for three business days from receipt. That right closes at the earlier of thirty days from acceptance or the closing date.

Give the form to buyers at the start of the listing so the cancellation clock never comes into play. Answer each item on it honestly and attach documents where you have them, such as repair invoices or permit records. A form filled in from memory invites follow-up questions, and a vague answer tends to cost more at the negotiating table than a plain one.

Build a folder before the first showing. Put in the signed state disclosure form, permits and final inspection records for any remodel, receipts for roof or HVAC work, and the association documents if your subdivision has one. Add the latest tax bill, which also shows the county that records your deed.

Buyers in a high-priced market read the paper trail closely. A clean folder answers most questions before they turn into price reductions, and it keeps an inspection report from becoming a negotiation over things you could have documented.

sections.h2: What to expect from contract to closing
sections.html:
Once you accept an offer, the title company confirms which county holds the deed, orders the property search and prepares the conveyance fee statement. Any open permit, unpaid association dues or recorded lien shows up in that search, so deal with those items early. Bring photo identification and any payoff letters to the signing.

A cash buyer removes the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which often makes the schedule shorter. The disclosure form, title search and recording still apply. Ask each buyer to put the price, the closing date and who pays each cost in writing, and compare offers on net proceeds rather than headline price.

faqs.q: Which county do I deal with when I sell a house in Dublin?
faqs.a: It depends on the parcel. Dublin falls within Franklin, Delaware, Union and Madison counties, so check your tax bill or the county auditor's property search to see which office records your deed.

faqs.q: Can I list my Dublin house on Airbnb to cover the mortgage while it sells?
faqs.a: Only with a city registration and within tight limits. Two weeks per calendar year is allowed, annual registration costs $225, and operating without registering carries a $250 fine.

faqs.q: How long do I have to fix a Dublin code violation?
faqs.a: Most notices give ten days, and code enforcement staff can extend that time when circumstances are unusual. Call Code Enforcement at 614.410.4600.

faqs.q: Does the city enforce my neighborhood's deed restrictions?
faqs.a: Generally not. The city lacks standing to pursue deed restrictions, so those fall to an association or neighbors. City zoning rules are separate.

faqs.q: What is Dublin's median home value?
faqs.a: The median value of an owner-occupied home is $563,500, and the owner-occupied rate is 77.1 percent.
